technical_and_design_decisions: For the Solo ordering service (U4), implement a simple single-process architecture using a buffered channel for client writes, a single thread for batching into blocks, and an in-RAM ledger with seek capability to handle history discovery without consensus.

For the CLI extraction (U8), design the peer commands as a standalone component with its own build process, ensuring it is independent of peer node internals like RocksDB, and can be compiled as platform-specific binaries for Mac and Windows.
Adopt modular development practices throughout to integrate new features such as friendly naming and lifecycle policies without disrupting existing Hyperledger Fabric components.
Use GitHub for code repository hosting (U5) to replace Gerrit, ensuring public access and ease of exploration for developers.
assumptions: I have full access to the existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase and development environment, including necessary tools and libraries.
The codebase is already structured in a modular way, allowing for relatively isolated changes for each user story.
Documentation work (U3, U7) can be completed using standard writing and publishing tools, with content hosted at hyperledger.org.
The GitHub repository setup (U5) involves standard git operations and can be completed efficiently without significant administrative overhead.
All development activities are performed by a single developer with expertise in Hyperledger Fabric, Go (primary language for Fabric), and related technologies.
Effort estimates are based on a standard 8-hour workday and include coding, testing, and basic integration, but exclude deployment to production or extensive user acceptance testing.

activities.activity_description: Add functionality to allow application developers to provide and manage friendly names for chaincodes, aiding in identification, management, and debugging. This involves changes to chaincode metadata and lifecycle processes.

Develop or enhance the lifecycle system to manage deployment policies for chaincodes, ensuring proper enforcement of policies during chaincode instantiation and upgrades. This may involve modifications to the lifecycle chaincode or system components.
Create comprehensive documentation detailing the steps, prerequisites, and best practices for upgrading Hyperledger Fabric components, including peers, orderers, and chaincodes.

Develop a minimal ordering service with a single process for easy deployment and testing. This includes implementing a buffered channel for client writes, a single thread for batching transactions into blocks, and an in-RAM ledger with seek capability to allow history discovery for disconnection/reconnection scenarios.

Transfer or set up the Hyperledger Fabric code repository on GitHub for public access, including configuring repository settings, migrating code from Gerrit if necessary, and ensuring developers can explore it without needing access to Gerrit.

Develop a state cache mechanism to provide quick access to the world state, helping submitters build read-write sets more efficiently and improving overall performance. This involves optimizing data access patterns and possibly integrating with existing state databases.

Compile and publish documentation for developing chaincodes and applications on Hyperledger Fabric, including tutorials, API references, and guides. Ensure the documentation is easily accessible at hyperledger.org and covers all Hyperledger Fabric projects.

Refactor the existing peer commands into a separate, standalone CLI component that can be installed independently on Mac and Windows. This involves decoupling the commands from peer internals, ensuring the CLI has no dependencies on RocksDB or other peer-specific libraries, and building platform-specific binaries.
